## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing respawn and render into a single pass over the AoS layout, with a 1-byte verdict intermediate, can amortize scatter cost and approach the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The 69 B/p AoS layout offers 28 hot bytes (41%) in loop 1 and 32 (47%) in loop 2 — over half each cache line is dead weight; the intermediate adds 1 B/p. Loop 1 gets partial auto-vectorization (vmulps/vaddps 4-wide within a particle), but fused loop 2 is scalar: 35 conditional branches, 31 byte-granular scatter stores, and a call to spawn. The working set spills L1d at N≈474 and L2 at N≈7598, but the 41-47% hot fraction extends effective residency beyond nominal.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p curve is strikingly flat: 21.989 ns/p at N=320 (L1d) to 25.038 ns/p at N=10M (DRAM) — ~14% rise across four orders of magnitude. No knee at L1d spill (N≈474) or L2 spill (N≈7598); a modest step at L3→DRAM (N=250K): ~23→25 ns/p at q=0.01. The flatness confirms the algo is not cache-bandwidth-limited — backend stalls (60-68%) dominate. The dense grid resolves the transitions but they are immaterial to cost.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 2.75-3.14 GB/s at q=0.01 — 22-25% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling. The 5.437 ns/p memory floor means the algo runs at 4-4.6x irreducible memory time. The verdict is backend-stall-bound (60-68%) with branch_flush rising from 11.5% (q=0.01) to 14.8% (q=0.5). It barely beats naive scalar: 0.93-0.99x at q=0.01, degrading to 0.91-1.01x at q=0.5. Against the winner it is 2.4-3.4x slower at q=0.01 and 1.8-2.1x slower at q=0.5 — the winner's LP2-opt avoids the 351-instruction fused body.

## Assembly
Loop 1 vectorizes partially: vmovups loads pos+vel, vmulps/vaddps do 4-wide FP, vinsertps/vshufps rearrange AoS, vmovlps writes back — but only within one particle; the mask write is setae+strb. Loop 2 is the bottleneck: 351 insns/iter, 35 cond branches, 31 byte-granular scatter stores. The scatter (movzx+add+cmp+cmovae+strb per R/G/B at multiple pixel offsets) cannot coalesce. The 12 cmovae color-clamp chains are branch-free but bounds-check branches dominate. Backend_stall of 60-68% reflects byte-store throughput limits.

## Verdict
Refuted — the fused scatter's byte-granular writes and 351-instruction loop body prevent any streaming benefit. At q=0.01 the algo is 0.93-0.99x of naive and 2.4-3.4x slower than the winner; at q=0.5 it is 0.91-1.01x of naive and 1.8-2.1x slower. Loop 1's component-wise auto-vectorization is negated by loop 2's 31 byte-granular scatter stores and 35 conditional branches, producing 60-68% backend stalls and capping bandwidth at 22-25% of ceiling. Rising branch_flush (11.5%→14.8%) erases even the marginal advantage over naive.
